palette.notes: Measured 4-28 colours per sheet: 1-bit 4, shine 9, silhouette 11, fundamentals 21, outlines 23, illumination 24, shading 27, fundamentals 2 28 (UI included). Strong warm hue shifts on skin and fur ramps (+51 to +64 deg) next to cool ones (-34 to -51 deg).

lighting: One clear light per object: a cube and a sphere lit from the top-left with a cast shadow, rim light against dark backgrounds, and coloured light from a source (lava, window, screen) that tints the side facing it.
silhouette: The silhouette sheet builds characters from a flat grey shape first (sketch, then details); a hero, an octopus monster and a round robot each read as a solid shape before any colour.

motion.timing: Mostly slideshow holds: fundamentals 70 frames at 130 ms, shading 7 drawings with 600 ms median holds, silhouette 1.8 s first hold, outlines 120 ms with 840 ms holds. Shine is the only motion: 80 ms sweep frames with 200-700 ms rests between glints.

texture: Dithering kept low (1.4-2.0%, 2.7% only in 1-bit where it stands in for grey); texture comes from clusters, not noise; the fundamentals panel warns against single stray pixels and jaggies.
camera: Static before/after panels: a wrong version beside the right one, or a sketch beside the finished sprite.

acting.enters: No characters enter; ideas are revealed one panel at a time, from silhouette to rendered sprite.
acting.acts: The demo objects change state instead of moving: the light source moves around a sphere, the outline switches from black to coloured, a glint sweeps across a sword.
acting.depth: Staging lesson: dark, low-contrast backgrounds behind high-contrast subjects; the 1-bit scene separates near and far using only pattern and line weight.

techniques: silhouette first: block the character as one flat shape that reads alone
one light source: highlight, mid, shadow, then a cast shadow on the ground
hue-shifted ramps: skin and fur go warmer in the light, cooler in the shadow
selective outline: coloured, darker on the shadow side, broken where light hits
rim light on the edge opposite the key light to separate from a dark background
shine sweep: a 2-3 px diagonal highlight crosses the object, then a long rest
1-bit: 4 colours, use dither and line weight for value
avoid pillow shading and single stray pixels
feel: one light + silhouette that reads in grey + selective coloured outline + a rare shine = solid sprites that stay clear at 1x
for_fred: Check Fred and Pixie as flat grey silhouettes at reel size before adding detail, and light them from one side with warm highlights and cool shadows. A shine sweep across Fred's scales, with a long rest between glints, is a cheap way to make him catch the eye when he comes back on screen.
